title: Rotating an array
questions: How do three in-place reversals rotate [A,B,C,D,E] right by 2 while restoring order within each moved group? What happens to the same elements during the three phases?

slide.title: Three reversals rotate the same array
slide.narrative:
The whole-array reversal puts the two groups in their final positions, but reverses the order inside each group. The next two reversals restore that order. All three operations change the same array, and the function returns that array.

For integer counts, normalization handles negative counts and counts larger than the array length. An empty array returns before normalization.

fileSummaries.summary: Rotation uses three in-place reversals instead of repeated pop/unshift operations.

inlineExplanations.text: Each element takes part in the whole-array reversal and one group reversal. The second reversal restores its order relative to other elements in its original group.

svgIllustration.title: Follow the same five elements
svgIllustration.takeaway: The whole-array reversal exchanges the groups and reverses their internal order. The next two reversals restore each group's order.
svgIllustration.assumptions: Input: [A,B,C,D,E], k = 2. Tile marks identify original groups. Off-row routes are schematic animation, not intermediate array contents, extra storage, or the literal order of individual swaps. Completed rows show the same array after each reversal.

plan.question: How do three reversals move [D,E] before [A,B,C] while restoring both groups' internal order?
plan.visualApproach: Keep five indexed array slots fixed and move the same marked tiles through three reversal phases. Separate each exchange into departure, horizontal crossing, and arrival so identities remain readable.
plan.whyThisForm: Fixed slots reveal changed positions, while persistent group marks reveal preserved membership. Completed rows expose how exchanging groups and restoring their internal order are separate effects.
plan.encodings: Horizontal position within the fixed row means array index. Solid tiles marked 1 belong to [A,B,C]; outlined tiles marked 2 belong to [D,E]. Off-row positions mean schematic movement only. The initial group split is n − k = 3; the subsequent reversal boundary is k = 2.
plan.motion: Indices and empty-slot outlines remain fixed. Tiles first leave the row vertically, cross in separate lanes below the index header, then arrive vertically at their destinations. C stays fixed during the whole-array reversal. Later phases move only D/E, then A/C. Introduce the k = 2 boundary only after the whole-array reversal has completed.
plan.prediction: For k = 1, E finishes at index 0. Reversing the remaining four positions restores [A,B,C,D] behind it.
plan.restingState: The final row shows [D,E | A,B,C], with the k = 2 boundary and original group marks still visible.
